objective: Test whether a fixed one-program-per-row RMSNormGated reduction preserves the accepted c1 arithmetic while removing the c2 row-shape-dependent output drift.
hypothesis: The generated dynamic persistent-reduction kernel changes reduction geometry with total packed row count. A Qwen-GDN-only kernel with one program per 128-element row and a fixed reduction order can make each row independent of neighboring requests without forcing c1 onto R91's rejected eager/custom-op arithmetic.

treatment.scope: Qwen RMSNormGated after the XPU GDN core, hidden width 128, SiLU gate, norm-before-gate only
arithmetic_contract: sum 128 squared values in one fixed Triton program
divide by 128, add the layer epsilon, and apply reciprocal square root
multiply by float32 norm weight and float32 SiLU(z)
store in the input dtype before the unchanged FP8 output projection

checks: a selected row is bitwise identical when evaluated alone and embedded in larger batches
candidate output is numerically consistent with RMSNormGated.forward_static on finite random inputs
unsupported shape or gating semantics fail closed rather than silently changing behavior

fixed_workload.sequence: Run cache-c000 alone at c1, then cache-c000 plus index-c001 at c2 on one fresh server and empty compile cache.

followup_if_pass: Build a non-tracing production-lineage image, repeat c1/c2 on a clean boot, then run the complete varied-prompt deterministic quality battery before any performance measurement or public change.
followup_if_fail: Preserve the result and use output digests to distinguish wrong c1 arithmetic, an inactive dispatch, or a remaining downstream boundary. Do not broaden the gate or promote throughput.
promotion_boundary: Diagnostic only. No public speed or quality authority; the current boot contains an earlier GPU reset.
